content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade to Apple's assistant, and it's now available on iOS 27. I noticed a standout difference between Siri AI and other AI assistants, and it's a good one.

The new Siri in iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, which is completely different from other AI chatbots.

Since the first beta of iOS 27 was released, I've been using Siri AI for almost four months. Overall, Siri AI has met all my expectations.

The new Siri is far better than its predecessor, finally delivering on the original promise of providing a capable assistant on Apple devices.

I have to admit that if you need the most cutting-edge, powerful AI tools out there, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might suit you better.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it with those third-party tools, I found one key difference that made me prefer Siri even more.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on long-winded speeches, mimic human personalities, or try to build a personal relationship with you.

Siri is helpful and smart, doing whatever you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows it's a tool, not a person. It frequently reminds you that it's an AI and can make mistakes. It also doesn't pretend to be in a relationship with you.

On the other hand, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are full of personality and opinions, presenting more human-like tendencies, but to me that feels really fake.

I know some users prefer that "humanised" approach. But I'd rather AI assistants just do their job without pretending to be something they're not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I really appreciate that Apple understands this and has designed the new Siri accordingly.

How "human-like" do you think AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
